definition: Keeping some layers (usually early ones) fixed during fine-tuning to preserve general features, cut compute, and reduce forgetting.
details: Keeping some layers (usually early ones) fixed during fine-tuning to preserve general features, cut compute, and reduce forgetting.

explainer.lead: Freezing layers locks part of a pretrained model during fine-tuning, cutting compute and protecting general features. It is a cheap way to adapt a large model to a small task.

tiers.eli5: Like keeping the foundation of a house when you redecorate: you only change the rooms you need.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers freeze early layers and train later ones, often with a lower learning rate; the pitfall is freezing too much, so the model cannot adapt to a task that differs from the original data.
tiers.paperLevel: Selected layers have their parameters held fixed (no gradient updates) while the remaining layers are optimized; the limit is that frozen features may not suit very different domains.

explainer.example: Fine-tuning an image classifier on a small medical dataset by freezing the early convolutional layers and training only the final classifier head.
